preamble.title: easy1staking-com/shithole
preamble.description: Shithole — Cardano dApp for swapping dead/rugpulled NFTs within their collection

aiken_merkle_tree/mt/Root.title: Root
aiken_merkle_tree/mt/Root.description:
An opaque root. Use [to_hash](#to_hash) and
 [from_hash](#from_hash) to convert back-and-forth between this and
 classic hashes. This type exists mainly to disambiguate between standard
 value (leaf) hash from tree hashes.

cardano/address/Address.title: Address
cardano/address/Address.description:
A Cardano `Address` typically holding one or two credential references.

 Note that legacy bootstrap addresses (a.k.a. 'Byron addresses') are
 completely excluded from Plutus contexts. Thus, from an on-chain
 perspective only exists addresses of type 00, 01, ..., 07 as detailed
 in [CIP-0019 :: Shelley Addresses](https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/tree/master/CIP-0019/#shelley-addresses).

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/PaymentCredential.title: PaymentCredential
cardano/address/PaymentCredential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/StakeCredential.title: StakeCredential
cardano/address/StakeCredential.description:
Represent a type of object that can be represented either inline (by hash)
 or via a reference (i.e. a pointer to an on-chain location).

 This is mainly use for capturing pointers to a stake credential
 registration certificate in the case of so-called pointer addresses.

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

anyOf.title: Deposit
anyOf.description:
Anyone-callable: caller adds `qty` of `(fee_token_policy, fee_token_name)`
 to the jar. `output_index` points to the continuing jar UTxO in
 `tx.outputs` for O(1) lookup.

anyOf.title: Sweep
anyOf.description:
Admin-only. Value distribution across the tx is admin's call (Cardano-
 level min-UTxO will fail the tx if the continuing UTxO falls below the
 protocol floor). The only structural invariants: admin signed, and at
 least one output exists at the jar address. This single redeemer covers
 both single-jar withdrawals AND multi-jar merges (N inputs -> M outputs,
 M < N) — the admin's signature subsumes any inter-input double-sat
 concern, so no per-input tag binding is needed on this path.

anyOf.title: Buy
anyOf.description:
Buyer fulfills the listing. Indexes hint O(1) lookup of the jar
 input/output and THIS listing's seller-payment output. In a bulk tx
 every Buy redeemer should carry the same `jar_input_index` and
 `jar_output_index` (off-chain consistency — each spend re-checks B4/B5
 against its own redeemer hints); `seller_output_index` differs per
 listing.

anyOf.title: Cancel
anyOf.description:
Seller withdraws. No output constraints — the seller signed; their
 asset, their call.

shithole/types/ConfigDatum.title: ConfigDatum
shithole/types/ConfigDatum.description:
Per-collection configuration.

 `collection_policy_id` is NOT a datum field — it lives as the config NFT's
 asset name (28 bytes, enforced at mint). Once minted it is immutable.

 `treasury_addr` should always be a base/payment-key address in practice
 (wallet, possibly HW). Script credentials are technically allowed but the
 script must accept payments with our tagged inline datum and not require
 any other signatures or datum fields — see SPEC §3.1 note.

shithole/types/ListingRedeemer.title: ListingRedeemer
shithole/types/ListingRedeemer.description:
Swap carries `nb_asset_name` (the NFT the swapper is depositing) and two
 output-index hints for O(1) lookup. NA's asset_name is read from the
 consumed listing's input value — not provided in the redeemer.

 The seed for the bucket equation is anchored to `own_ref` (the consumed
 listing's outRef), not to a swapper-controlled input. This makes the swap
 outcome a deterministic function of (consumed listing, deposited NFT)
 pairs — the swapper has no per-attempt manipulation axis. For dead
 collections this is the desired property.

 Recover is an admin-only rescue path for UTxOs that landed at the listing
 address with NO datum (e.g. someone pay-to-script'd by accident). Datum
 is required to be `None` — admin has no power over any datum-bearing UTxO.
 Validator pulls `admin_pkh` from the per-collection config (read as ref
 input, same lookup pattern as Swap).

shithole/types/WantedRedeemer.title: WantedRedeemer
shithole/types/WantedRedeemer.description:
Redeemer for the wanted-listing validator.

 `Fulfill` is the happy path: seller deposits a trait-matching NFT and
 receives the offered NFT + bounty.

 `Reclaim` lets the buyer pull their offered NFT + bounty back out of
 the listing. Authorized by `signed_by(buyer_pkh)`.

 `Rescue` is the admin-only path for UTxOs that landed at the wanted-
 listing address with NO datum (someone pay-to-script'd by accident).
 Strictly requires `datum == None` — the admin has zero power over any
 datum-bearing UTxO. Same semantics as v2 `ListingRedeemer::Recover`;
 renamed here because Aiken's constructor names are module-level and
 would collide with the v2 listing redeemer's `Recover`.

fields.title: merkle_proof
fields.description:
Merkle membership proof of the deposited NFT's `asset_name` against
 `WantedDatum.accepted_merkle_root`. Built off-chain via the
 `aiken_merkle_tree/mt` library's `get_proof`; verified on-chain
 via `mt.is_member`. Each ProofItem is a directional `Left(Root)`
 or `Right(Root)`. Hashing is sha2_256; leaf = sha2_256(asset_name).

fields.title: treasury_output_index
fields.description:
Some(idx) ⇒ outputs[idx] is the treasury payment, validated against
 cfg.protocol_fee + the compute_output_tag(own_ref) anti-double-sat
 tag. None ⇒ no treasury output supplied; validator requires
 `cfg.protocol_fee == 0`.
